proposals.warning: At the Q3 2026 filing scheduled for **29 October 2026**, trigger a full re-read if transaction-fee revenue growth trails total ADV growth by **15 percentage points or more** while total variable fees per million also decline by **more than 10% year on year**. proposals.break: At the FY2026 10-K, to be checked by **1 March 2027**, put the position under §5.1 if two consecutive quarters have both (a) flat or declining transaction-fee revenue despite positive ADV growth and (b) year-on-year declines in Tradeweb's fully electronic U.S. high-grade and high-yield TRACE shares. proposals.warning: In the Q3 FY2027 filing scheduled for **17 November 2026**, trigger a full re-read if quarter-end receivable days exceed **65 days** (`accounts receivable ÷ quarterly revenue × 91`, versus 59.6 days now), or if any disclosed customer-support category—equity investments and commitments, AI-cloud agreements and third-party leases, or guarantees—grows by more than **20%** while Data Center revenue grows more slowly. This is the earliest disclosed evidence that credit and support may be pulling demand forward; it is not an automatic sale ([Q2 filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000075/nvda-20260726.htm), [local result date](../../prices.json)).
proposals.break: By the FY2027 annual filing, checkable on **1 March 2027**, put the position under §5.1 if NVIDIA reports a material customer or partner default, a called guarantee, or a credit-loss provision tied to these support arrangements. It also breaks if receivable days remain above 65 for two consecutive quarters **and** a support category continues growing faster than Data Center revenue in both. NVIDIA does not disclose how much revenue comes from customers it invests in, finances or guarantees, so the central circular-demand risk is **not fully falsifiable today**; the £75 size is the cost of that missing disclosure.
